prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological insulator, a new topological class of electronic matter.

statement.case_for: I opened with B008 (KPZ) because it is the cleanest example of a minimal model defining a universality class, but after reading the other seven ballots I move B057 to the front of my configuration. It is the one candidate that combines a decisive, model-level theoretical idea (Kane and Mele's Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant insulators and the quantum spin Hall proposal) with an unambiguous, quantitative experimental realisation (Molenkamp's HgTe edge-channel conductance), and it has the widest support across the committee: all seven colleagues who ranked it did so, and Eriksson placed it first. The mechanism is general, band topology protecting edge states without symmetry breaking, and has been confirmed by transport, ARPES and many material families for about two decades. It is also a clean three-person theory-plus-experiment trio, which is not true of most of the list.
statement.case_against: The 2016 prize for topological phase transitions and topological phases of matter (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz) already covers part of the conceptual ground, and the committee would need to articulate what the Z2 and spin-Hall step adds. The credit is also genuinely contested: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe quantum-well realisation that Molenkamp measured, Zhang has died, and the three-dimensional topological-insulator work (Fu, Kane, Mele; Moore, Balents; Hasan) is outside the credited set. Compared with B027, the attribution is less crisp and the timeliness argument is weaker.

responses.point: Ranks B057 first as a verified, quantitatively predicted discovery of a new class of quantum matter, with a natural theory-plus-experiment trio and a mature, overdue field.
responses.response: I agree on the science and on the structure of the trio, and I think the strongest answer to the 2016 overlap is that Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz honoured topological invariants in specific models and phase transitions, whereas Kane-Mele and Molenkamp gave a symmetry-protected classification of real band insulators with a decisive measurement. My reservation is that predicting HgTe quantitatively was the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang step, so I would ask you whether the citation can be framed around the Z2 concept and the observation without implying that the HgTe prediction is unrecognised.

responses.point: Ranks the optical lattice clock (B027) first as the clearest case of a measurement technique that changed what can be measured, mature and independently confirmed worldwide, with a clean two-person credit.
responses.response: I take B027 seriously; it has the best attribution and timing on the list and I left it off my own opening ballot, which I now think was too narrow. Where I differ is that I would not let a clean credit decide the matter, since a clean credit is partly a consequence of a small number of people on a technique. Still, I regard B027 as a fully legitimate winner, which is why I list it as an alternative, and if the committee prefers it I could not make a scientific case against it.

responses.point: Ranks circuit QED (B036) first as a new regime of strong single-photon coupling and the architecture behind superconducting processors, and defers partly to condensed-matter colleagues on B057 while flagging the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission as a real credit dispute.
responses.response: I accept your credit point on B057 and do not think it can be waved away, but it applies to the choice of names rather than to the discovery. On B036, I am concerned that the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits already recognises the superconducting-circuit platform, and I would want to hear what the new physics is beyond the architecture; I would not support B036 ahead of B057 on the present arguments.

responses.point: Ranks aberration-corrected electron microscopy (B053) first as an enabling instrument breakthrough with a natural Rose, Haider, Urban split, and places B057 at rank 7, relying on colleagues for condensed-matter judgement.
responses.response: The instrument case is real and the maturity is beyond doubt, but I would ask whether it is a physics discovery or an enabling technique whose scientific output is spread over materials science, and I note that only you and Olsson, who has declared an interest, ranked it. I would not oppose it as a second part of a prize, though the three-person limit makes combining B053 with another trio impossible unless names are cut.

uncertainties: Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize makes a second topology award feel incremental to the full committee.
Whether the credit should be reshaped to reflect Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and whether a three-name union can be defended without them.
Whether B008 (KPZ) can be considered at all, given that Parisi, co-author of the original equation and a 2021 laureate, is not in the credited names and that my opening was the only support for it.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B057, B008 or B027. I am in the Gothenburg physics environment with Johansson and Olsson (Chalmers), who rank other candidates, but I have no known collaboration with any credited person on these ballots.
